title: throw versus throw ex (preserving the stack trace)
hook: throw; rethrows and keeps the original stack trace. throw ex; looks similar but destroys the evidence. Wrapping with InnerException is a third move — add context once at a boundary.

blocks.text: Inside a catch block, **throw;** (no identifier) rethrows the current exception and **preserves StackTrace**. **throw ex;** starts a new throw site — StackTrace now begins in your catch, and the original frames from Redis, SkiaSharp, or the database driver are lost or harder to read. A third pattern wraps: **throw new DomainException("context", ex);** where **InnerException** keeps the root cause. Wrap once at a semantic boundary, not at every layer.

entries.plainDefinition: Rethrows the exception currently being handled. Preserves the original stack trace.
Throws the caught variable as a new throw. Resets StackTrace to the current location — the classic bug.
entries.example: catch (Exception ex) { throw ex; } // loses original frames

entries.plainDefinition: Links a wrapping exception to its root cause. Walk ex.InnerException to see the chain.
Captures an exception and rethrows it later without resetting the stack — for delayed rethrow outside catch.

blocks.text: Production debugging depends on StackTrace pointing at the real failure site. throw ex; in a worker turns a one-line Redis timeout into "failed in CatchAllHandler line 42" with no Redis frames. Interviewers ask this in the first ten seconds because it separates people who copy-paste catch blocks from people who understand CLR behavior.

blocks.title: Log and throw; — do not wrap just to log
blocks.body: If you only need logging, log inside catch and throw;. Wrapping adds noise unless the caller needs a domain-level type like TokenValidationException.

items.title: throw; inside catch
items.body: Use when you logged or cleaned up but cannot recover. StackTrace stays intact.

items.title: throw new OuterException(msg, inner)
items.body: Use at a boundary when the caller should see a domain type. InnerException preserves the root.

items.title: ExceptionDispatchInfo for delayed throw
items.body: When you store an exception and throw later outside a catch block, Capture().Throw() preserves the stack.

items.title: Never throw ex;
items.body: There is no legitimate production use. If you see it in a code review, replace with throw;.

diagram.title: Stack trace preservation
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  A[Failure in ParseCore] --> B{catch block}
  B -->|throw;| C[StackTrace includes ParseCore]
  B -->|throw ex;| D[StackTrace starts at catch line]
  B -->|wrap with InnerException| E[Outer stack + InnerException chain]

snippet.explanation: Line 8: wrap JSON failures once with InnerException so callers see InvalidOperationException. Line 14: after logging, throw; keeps the original timeout frames. throw ex; would erase them.

snippet.label: Walking the InnerException chain
snippet.explanation: Line 3: loop from outer to inner. Line 11: the outer message is domain-friendly; the inner message has the parser detail.

snippet.label: ExceptionDispatchInfo for delayed rethrow
snippet.explanation: Line 7: throw; only works physically inside catch. ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture preserves the stack when you must throw later from a different method.

blocks.title: Rethrow and wrap in C# vs JS/TS
rows: throw; preserves stack; throw ex; resets it
throw e typically keeps the same Error object and stack
Re-throw the same Error object — stack usually preserved
throw ex; is a well-known C# bug
Less common — no separate stack-reset rule

blocks.title: catch (Exception ex) { throw ex; }
blocks.body: This pattern appears in old tutorials and production workers. Replace every instance with throw;. Your on-call engineer will thank you.

blocks.title: Wrapping at every layer
blocks.body: Five nested InvalidOperationException wrappers make logs unreadable. Wrap once at the API boundary; inner layers log and throw;.

interviewTakeaways: throw; preserves StackTrace. throw ex; resets it.
Wrap with InnerException at a semantic boundary, once.
ExceptionDispatchInfo for delayed rethrow outside catch.
commonPitfalls: catch (Exception ex) { throw ex; } in production workers.
Wrapping the same exception at five layers until logs are unreadable.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript throw e typically keeps the error object; there is no separate throw versus throw e stack-reset rule like C#'s throw ex. Error.cause is the modern wrap.
new Error(msg, { cause }) is the JavaScript/TypeScript wrap. C# uses InnerException on Exception constructors.
